ruminal bacteria have cell-associated carboxymethyl cellulases (CMCases) and that these enzymes play a role in the digestion of β-glucan in the rumen.

(i) ruminal bacteria can degrade β-glucans by a mechanism that includes cell-associated CMCase activity, (ii) the cellulolytic and β-glucanylizing bacteria are similar with respect to their CMCase and βglucanase activities, and (iii) the CMCase activity of mixed ruminal bacterial populations was correlated with the β-glucan utilization by these bacteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of ruminal bacteria in the degradation of cereal grains and in particular the role of carboxymethyl cellulases in the degradation β-glucans in the cereal grains.
the role of ruminal cellulolytic bacteria and their cellulases in the degradation and utilization of cereal grain.
the role of cellulolytic bacteria in the degradation of cell wall carbohydrates in the rumen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the CMCase activity of ruminal bacteria provides a mechanism for utilizing soluble β-1,4 linked glucans (cellulose, mixed β-1-3,1-4 glucans, and soluble β-1-4 glucan) from cereal grains, but does not appear to play a major role in the utilization of cellulose.
the CMCase activity of ruminal bacteria is a major factor influencing the degradation of β-1, 3-1, 4 glucans from cereal grains.
ruminal carboxy-methylcellulase activity is a good indicator of β-glucan utilization by ruminal bacteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cellulolytic bacteria are the major source of β-glucanases, but they are not the only source.
the cellulolytic and hemicellulolytic bacteria of the rumen can be grouped according to their ability to degrade cellulose and β-glucans.
cellulases, especially carboxymethyl cellulases (CMCases) are important in the degradation of cereal β-glucans by ruminal microorganisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ruminal bacteria have multiple mechanisms for degrading cellulose and hemicellulose, but the CMCase activity of ruminal bacteria is not required to grow on cellulose.
the CMCase activity of ruminal bacteria is important for the degradation of water soluble β-glucose polymers.
the CMCase activity of ruminal bacteria is a key factor determining the extent to which they degrade β-glucans in cereal grain.
